sentences.text: ORDER This misc. appeal u/S. 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 198 has been filed by appellants- claimants seeking enhancement of compensation amount by taking exception to the Award dated 06/03/2019 passed by Member, MACT, District-Shivpuri (M.P.) (in short "Claims Tribunal") in Claim Case No.238/2018, whereby the Claims Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs. 6,00,900/- along with interest from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization in favour of claimants on account of death of Brijlal Jatav in a motor accident.
2. The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard are not in question.
3 . Counsel for appellants submitted that the Claims Tribunal has committed an error in awarding compensation amount by not examining the evidence properly.

Learned Claims Tribunal has also committed an error in NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:24847 2 MA-3164-2019 not awarding any future prospect in favour of claimants as well as adopting the age of deceased between 51 to 55 years for which multiplier of "11" has been applied wrongly.
The findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal with regard to income of deceased is also not correct in the eye of law by assessing income at Rs. 6000/- per month.

Learned counsel for the appellants/claimants further contended that Claims Tribunal has committed an error in not awarding reasonable amount in other heads i.e.
loss of estate, loss of consortium, funeral expenses etc.

Hence, it is prayed that reasonable amount of Smt.Bhabuti vs Shyam Sundar Pal on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77416938/
1 compensation may be awarded to the claimants.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company contended that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation and argued in support of the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal.

5. Heard the arguments advanced by the counsel for the parties and perused the record of the Tribunal.
6.
After hearing counsel for the parties, it is found that Claims Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased is on lower side.

In considered opinion of this Court, the just and proper amount of the income of the deceased as per Minimum Wages Act in the present case is Rs. 7,125/- per month of an unskilled labour instead of Rs.6000/- per month which has wrongly been assessed by the Claims Tribunal.

7. As regards loss of income including future prospects, in the light of judgment of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi , 2017 ACJ 2700 , NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:24847 3 MA-3164-2019 the claimants are entitled for loss of income including future prospects of 10% and as per the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors.

Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, even if age of the deceased is to be taken into account, multiplier of "11" has been rightly applied by the Claims Tribunal and personal expenses 1/3 of deceased has rightly been deducted by the Claims Tribunal.
8.

Accordingly, appellants- claimants are entitled to get compensation under the following heads:-
 HEAD AMOUNT  Rs 7,125/- per month X12=85  Income  annum  Future Prospects@10% Rs. 8,550/-

Total income Rs.94,050/-
 Dependency 2/3 Rs.62,700/-
 Loss of Income Rs.62,700X11= 6,89,700/-
Other Heads:-

Loss of Consortium Rs.40,000 X 4 = Rs. 1,60,0  Loss of Estate and funeral  Rs.30,000/-
 expenses
Total Compensation = Rs 9.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case i s Rs.8,79,700/- as against the Award of the Claims Tribunal of Rs. 6,00,900/-.
Accordingly, the appellants/claimants are entitled to an additional sum of Rs. 2,78,800/- over and above the amount, which has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal.

2 10.

In the result, this miscellaneous appeal is partly allowed, by NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:24847 4 MA-3164-2019 enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.
2,78,800/-.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest as fixed by the learned Claims Tribunal from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization.
The said amount be paid within a period of three months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
Rest of conditions as imposed by learned Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

11. If the enhanced amount of compensation is in excess to the valuation of appeal, the difference of the Court fee (if not already paid) shall be deposited by the appellants- claimants within a period of one month and proof thereof, shall be submitted before the Registry.
Thereafter, the Registry shall issue the certified copy of the order passed today.
12. In view of the above, miscellaneous appeal filed by the appellants/claimants stands disposed of.
